# Independently verify dungeon encounters

Use a separate reviewer context from the author. Read the completed candidates,
current objectives, retrieved official source evidence and maintenance policy.
Re-evaluate every correct option, distractor, explanation, prerequisite, code
operation, feature status and citation relevance. Do not trust the author's key.

Write a question-specific ledger attestation for every candidate/status. Bind the
exact question fingerprint and current source snapshots. Record each option's
support/contradiction/ambiguity and documented rationale. Resolve blocking
duplicates and inspect editorial warnings. Reject unsupported or ambiguous facts.

Separately score all ten realism criteria in the encounter envelope. Each score
is 0–2 with actual reviewer identity, review timestamp and item-specific notes.
Passing requires at least 18/20, no zero, and 2 for accuracy, uniqueness and
documentation strength. A hash or passing structural test is not a review.

Re-read the actual current competency outline and bind the rubric itself using
required `objectiveVersion` and `objectiveFingerprint` fields.
`objectiveFingerprint(taxonomy)` is exported by the shared and script review
helpers. It hashes the version, exact guide URL and complete ordered objective
map, excluding retrieval time. Record your actual review timestamp at or after
the taxonomy retrieval. Never renew old rubrics by changing envelope versions,
hashes or dates without a new independent outline review.

Populate source IDs, exact per-option attestation rationales, retrieval/validation
snapshots and objectiveVersion in `encounter-metadata.json`. No command generates
these attestations for you. Never invent evidence, current status or review dates.
